title: Candidates and short lines
outcomes: Writes a short candidate list (forcing moves first)
Follows each candidate for about three plies and drops the ones that fail
Holds a position in the head well enough to list a piece's legal moves with pieces hidden
Knows what a short line can miss

steps.text: Do not play the first good-looking move. Make a short **candidate list**: two to four moves, forcing moves first. Then follow each for about three **plies** (a ply is one move by one side): your move, the opponent's best reply, your next move. Drop candidates that clearly fail. Two to four is a habit to try, not a rule.

steps.caption: White is in check. The candidate list is short: White has exactly four legal moves.

line.say: Black takes the rook with check.
Bxd1 takes the queen. Three plies show White clearly ahead.

claims.statement: White has exactly four legal moves: Kg1, Be2, Qxc4 and Qd3.
Qxc4 is the engine's best move.
Qxc4 nets White at least five points of material along the engine's line.

steps.text: To follow a line you must hold the board in your head. **Drill:** you study a position for 15 seconds, then some pieces vanish from the board. You must still say where a piece can go. This is a training exercise for seeing lines, not a chess rule.

**Short lines have limits.** Three plies are enough when every move is forcing. They can mislead when a sacrifice pays off later: a line that looks bad at ply three can be mate at ply five. And in quiet positions the candidates may not separate at all.
Ask: **is the last move of my line quiet or forcing?**

steps.text: **What the app does for you now, and when it stops.** Here a candidate-list box sits beside the board. In mixed practice it is hidden; you can open it and the app notes that you did. The plan: stop showing it once you solve five mixed items in a row without it (five is a first guess). Next item is silent: you keep your list and lines in your head.

steps.prompt: Before you moved in the silent item, how sure were you? Then write your candidate list from memory, and name the first move you considered and the reply that made you drop it.
